BSS school buzzed with color and thread in early August as seven AquaTerra volunteers guided two hundred children through the Sacred Strings Rakhi-making workshop. Ribbons, beads, and a lot of concentration went into each handmade rakhi.

With one of the largest turnouts in this project set, the day was busy but joyful, each child leaving with a rakhi tied not just for the wrist but for the bonds it was meant to represent.

header: Tails and Treats - Feeding Stray Dogs 30.0
short_summary: Volunteers fed street dogs with biscuits, continuing efforts to care for animals in the community.
long_writeup:
Five AquaTerra volunteers walked the lanes of Salt Lake this March, biscuit packets in hand, making sure fifty-five street dogs didn't go hungry that day. It's quiet, unglamorous work, but the dogs recognize the routine by now.

Marking the 30th edition of Tails and Treats, the drive is proof that small, repeated acts of care add up to something the neighborhood's strays can count on.

header: Wear and Share - Clothes Collection Drive 19.0
short_summary: Uniting hearts through clothes, spreading warmth one piece at a time.
long_writeup:
Three AquaTerra volunteers spent time at Club Town Greens in July gathering clothes for the 19th edition of Wear and Share, collecting eight kilograms to pass along to those who could use them.

It wasn't a large haul, but every piece collected means one less family going without. The drive continues quietly, one neighborhood and one bag of clothes at a time.

header: Food For All - Food Distribution Drive 1.0
short_summary: Distributed bananas as part of a food drive to support the underprivileged.
long_writeup:
Near Shiv Temple in Salt Lake, four AquaTerra volunteers kicked off the first edition of Food For All by handing out six hundred bananas to those in need. The line moved steadily, and so did the bananas.

It was a straightforward morning of service, the kind that doesn't need embellishment. Nutrition and dignity, delivered one banana at a time, set the tone for the editions that would follow.
label_2: For the ones who need it the most.

header: Bottle To Better - Upcycling Bottle Workshop
short_summary: This hands-on workshop focused on upcycling discarded plastic bottles into practical and decorative items.
long_writeup: This hands-on workshop focused on upcycling discarded plastic bottles into practical and decorative items. Children and volunteers worked together to transform waste into pencil holders, planters, and bird feeders, showing that sustainability can be both fun and creative. Alongside the activity, discussions were held on the harmful effects of plastic pollution and the importance of reducing, reusing, and recycling in daily life. The session empowered participants with both awareness and action, encouraging them to become conscious changemakers within their homes and communities.

short_summary: Participants learned to speak with clarity, poise, and impact.
long_writeup:
Ek Tara hosted forty eager voices this May, as four AquaTerra volunteers ran the Voice Power workshop on public speaking. Children took turns at the front of the room, practicing eye contact, pacing, and the nerve it takes to speak up.

By the end, the shy ones weren't quite so shy, and the confident ones were sharper still. Public speaking is a skill that pays off for years, and this session gave forty kids a real head start on it.

short_summary: Shared 20L of Rooh Afza with locals in a summer relief drive by 8 volunteers.
long_writeup:
Howrah's March heat met its match when eight AquaTerra volunteers rolled out the 23rd Sharbat Seva drive, pouring twenty liters of Rooh Afza for anyone passing by in need of a cool break.

With a bigger volunteer turnout than usual, the team moved quickly, making sure the sharbat reached as many people as possible before it ran out. Small relief, delivered with a smile, on a day that called for both.

short_summary: A skill-building workshop at Disha engaging children in interactive learning and development.
long_writeup:
Two AquaTerra volunteers spent an April afternoon at Disha Foundation running Word Play, an English workshop built around games rather than grammar drills. Twenty-five children jumped into word games, spelling challenges, and a fair bit of laughter.

Language sticks better when it's fun, and that was the whole idea here. The session left the children a little more confident with English and a lot more willing to speak up in it.

header: Merry Miracles Drive of Christmas Carnival at Sunday School Day 4
short_summary: Day 4 of Merry Miracles: A joyful Christmas carnival with games, music, and festive cheer for kids.
long_writeup:
The Merry Miracles series wrapped its fourth day at Pather Sathi with five AquaTerra volunteers turning the space into a mini Christmas carnival. Thirty-five children played games, sang along to festive tunes, and soaked up the holiday spirit.

After three days of build-up, this final carnival day was pure celebration, closing out the series on a note of laughter and shared joy rather than a lesson plan.

header: Colours Of Durga - Durga Puja Workshop at Sunday School 4.0
short_summary: The final Durga Puja workshop with Pather Sathi was a vibrant culmination of festive learning and joy.
long_writeup: The final Durga Puja workshop with Pather Sathi was a vibrant culmination of festive learning and joy. Children participated in devotional singing, shared folk tales around the goddess, and created festive crafts like paper garlands and puja cards. Volunteers facilitated group reflections on the significance of Durga's triumph and the relevance of strength, protection, and unity in their own lives. The session radiated warmth, laughter, and pride in cultural heritage. It was more than just a workshop, it was a celebration of spirit, identity, and collective memory that beautifully closed the Puja series.

header: Splash of Joy - Holi Workshop at Sunday School
short_summary: Sunday School Holi workshop filled with colours, crafts, and joyful celebration of the festival.
long_writeup:
Color took over Pather Sathi this March as five AquaTerra volunteers ran a Holi-themed workshop for thirty-five children, mixing craft-making with the sheer joy of the festival. Hands turned every shade by the end of it.

Splash of Joy leaned into what Holi does best: bringing people together without much formality. Between the crafts and the color, the session was as much about play as it was about celebrating tradition.

short_summary: Held in collaboration with Youthwave and South Calcutta Inner Wheel School, the Rakhi Workshop brought together creativity, culture, and community spirit.
long_writeup: Held in collaboration with Youthwave and South Calcutta Inner Wheel School, the Rakhi Workshop brought together creativity, culture, and community spirit. Children participated in making beautiful, handmade rakhis using eco-friendly materials, guided by enthusiastic volunteers. Alongside the art, the session explored the deeper meaning of Raksha Bandhan, celebrating bonds of love, protection, and unity. The workshop also encouraged sustainable practices by promoting reuse of materials and reducing waste. It was a joyful, hands-on experience that blended tradition with creativity, leaving the children proud of their work and more connected to the cultural roots of the festival.

short_summary: Nutritious meals distributed to those in need with care and compassion.
long_writeup:
As part of the Paradox initiative, three AquaTerra volunteers spent a December day in Kolkata handing out sixty food packets to people who needed a warm, nutritious meal. No fanfare, just food reaching hands that needed it.

It was the first day of the drive, setting a steady, practical tone: show up, distribute what you can, and let the meals speak for the effort behind them.

short_summary: Volunteers served 20 liters of Rooh Afza sharbat to beat the heat and refresh the community.
long_writeup:
Five AquaTerra volunteers set up in Topsia this March for the 18th edition of Sharbat Seva, ladling out twenty liters of Rooh Afza to anyone looking for a break from the heat.

The drive has become something of a fixture by its 18th round, a small but reliable point of relief for the neighborhood each time the volunteers show up with their jugs and cups ready.

header: Christmas Carols - Workshop at Sunday School 1.0
short_summary: Festive carols workshop at Sunday School where kids sang, learned tunes, and spread cheer.
long_writeup:
Pather Sathi opened its Christmas season this December with three AquaTerra volunteers leading twenty-five children through carols old and new. Voices cracked, tunes wobbled, and everyone had a great time anyway.

As the first in the Christmas Carols series, this session set a warm, musical tone for the workshops to follow, proving that a shared song can bring a room together faster than almost anything else.

short_summary: Roots tees making their mark on Calcutta Boys School - Concord Day 1.
long_writeup:
Calcutta Boys School saw a big turnout as ten AquaTerra volunteers kicked off Day 1 of Concord with the Roots initiative, drawing two hundred walk-ins over the course of the event.

With the largest volunteer team in this batch of projects, the day ran smoothly from setup to close, marking a strong start to what Concord had planned across its first day.

short_summary: Building confidence and skills, one lesson at a time.
long_writeup:
Three AquaTerra volunteers returned to Pather Sathi this July for another round of Happy Hands, working with thirty children on lessons designed to build both skills and self-assurance.

These recurring sessions are less about a single big moment and more about steady presence, showing up again and again so the children know the volunteers, and the learning, will keep coming back.

short_summary: Organized in collaboration with Ek Tara, the Dental Camp Workshop focused on promoting oral hygiene among children.
long_writeup: Organized in collaboration with Ek Tara, the Dental Camp Workshop focused on promoting oral hygiene among children. The session included basic dental checkups, interactive demonstrations on brushing techniques, and fun activities to teach the importance of daily dental care. Dentists and volunteers explained the link between oral health and overall well-being in simple, engaging ways. The children actively participated, asked questions, and received free dental kits to take home. The workshop helped reduce fear around dental visits while encouraging lifelong healthy habits. It was both educational and empowering for the young attendees.

header: Grow and Glow - Workshop at Sunday School
short_summary: A Sunday school workshop introducing children to basics of digital literacy and computer skills.
long_writeup: At the Sunday school computer workshop, our team introduced children to the basics of digital literacy - from identifying computer parts to using educational software. Many of these children had never interacted with a computer before, so this hands-on exposure opened a new world of learning for them. The session focused on building confidence with technology in a fun, engaging, and age-appropriate way. It was heartening to witness their curiosity and excitement as they explored tools that could empower their future education and opportunities.

header: Young Minds - Workshop at Sunday School
short_summary: Engaging Sunday School workshop with stories, games, and learning for young curious minds.
long_writeup:
Four AquaTerra volunteers spent a December session at Pather Sathi mixing stories, games, and gentle learning for thirty young minds eager for both. Young Minds kept the pace light while still leaving room for real engagement.

It's the kind of workshop that doesn't announce itself as important, but the steady rhythm of games and stories is exactly what keeps children coming back to Sunday school week after week.

header: Tails and Treats - Feeding Stray Dogs 28.0
short_summary: Volunteers fed biscuits to street dogs, spreading care and compassion through a dog drive.
long_writeup:
The 28th edition of Tails and Treats brought seven AquaTerra volunteers to Salt Lake Haveli this March, biscuits in tow for sixty-five street dogs who'd come to expect the visit.

Feeding drives like this rarely make headlines, but the dogs notice the consistency, and so does the neighborhood. It's care delivered quietly, one biscuit and one wagging tail at a time.

header: Cycle of Care - Sanitary Napkin Distribution
short_summary: Sanitary napkins were distributed by volunteers to women near a slum area to promote hygiene.
long_writeup:
Two AquaTerra volunteers spent time at Salt Lake Haveli this March distributing eighty packets of sanitary napkins to women in a nearby slum area, addressing a need that too often goes unspoken.

Cycle of Care is built around dignity as much as hygiene, making sure something as basic as access to sanitary products isn't a barrier for the women who received these packets.

header: Merry Miracles Drive of Christmas Crafts Day 1
short_summary: Day 1 of Merry Miracles: Kids created joyful Christmas crafts, embracing colour, fun, and festivity.
long_writeup:
The Merry Miracles series kicked off at Ek Tara this December, with two AquaTerra volunteers helping thirty children get crafty with colorful Christmas decorations. Glue, glitter, and holiday cheer covered the tables by the end.

As the opening day of a multi-part series, this session set the festive mood early, giving the children something to be proud of and look forward to as the celebrations continued.

short_summary: Old tees, new stories - creativity stitched with purpose.
long_writeup:
Ten AquaTerra volunteers brought a stack of old t-shirts to Mahadevi Birla Sishu Vihar this April, turning ReTee into a hands-on lesson in upcycling for thirty-five children. Scissors, fabric paint, and a bit of imagination did the rest.

With one of the largest volunteer teams in recent memory, the session moved at a good clip, giving every child a chance to turn a worn-out tee into something new. It was as much about sustainability as it was about creative fun.

header: Colours Of Durga - Durga Puja Workshop at Sunday School 5.0
short_summary: The October session marked the closing chapter of our Durga Puja workshop series with Pather Sathi.
long_writeup: The October 8th session marked the closing chapter of our Durga Puja workshop series with Pather Sathi. Children immersed themselves in festive activities, creating colorful artwork, singing devotional songs, and sharing what the goddess Durga meant to them. The workshop focused on expression, celebration, and connection, blending creative arts with cultural storytelling. Volunteers encouraged conversations on themes like inner strength, courage, and community bonding. The session wrapped up with joyful energy and a shared sense of pride in tradition. It was a fitting finale that left every child smiling and inspired.

header: Merry Miracles Drive of Dental Checkup Day 2
short_summary: Day 2 of Merry Miracles: Free dental checkups for kids promoting hygiene and healthy smiles.
long_writeup:
Gyan Deepak hosted Day 2 of Merry Miracles this December, with three AquaTerra volunteers running free dental checkups for thirty children as part of the wider celebration.

Between the festive activities of the series, this session carved out space for something practical, giving children and their families a simple, useful health check alongside all the holiday cheer.

header: Christmas Carols Workshop at Sunday School 2.0
short_summary: Kids learned classic Christmas carols, spreading festive joy through song at Sunday School.
long_writeup:
Following the series opener, two AquaTerra volunteers returned to Pather Sathi for the second round of Christmas Carols, teaching twenty-five children a fresh set of tunes to sing.

By now the children knew the drill, and the singing came easier. It was a short, cheerful session that added another layer of festive spirit to the Sunday school calendar.

header: Learning Lights - Workshop at Sunday School
short_summary: In collaboration with Pather Sathi, this Sunday school workshop offered children a space to learn, express, and grow.
long_writeup: In collaboration with Pather Sathi, this Sunday school workshop offered children a space to learn, express, and grow. The session blended creative activities like drawing and storytelling with conversations on kindness, empathy, and teamwork. Volunteers helped facilitate engaging games and exercises that encouraged confidence and collaboration. The goal was to nurture a sense of values alongside fun and imagination. With Pather Sathi's involvement, the workshop added a layer of community connection, emphasizing how local partnerships can enrich learning environments for children in meaningful ways.

header: Paint the Planet - Earth Day Art Workshop
short_summary: Children created Earth Day-themed art, learning about nature, conservation, and self-expression.
long_writeup:
Amader Pradakhep turned into an open-air studio this March, as two AquaTerra volunteers led twenty-five children through an Earth Day art session. Paints, nature sketches, and conversations about conservation filled the afternoon.

Paint the Planet used art as the entry point, but the real lesson was environmental: children left with a better sense of why the planet is worth looking after, expressed in their own colors.

short_summary: Brightening lives through education and care.
long_writeup:
Six AquaTerra volunteers filled Pather Sathi with energy this July for Joy Jam, working with forty children on a mix of learning and playful engagement.

With a solid volunteer turnout, the session moved easily between structured learning and lighter moments, leaving the children both a little wiser and a lot more cheerful by the end of it.

header: Food For All - Food Distribution Drive 2.0
short_summary: Distributed bananas to support nutrition and hunger relief in the community.
long_writeup:
Three AquaTerra volunteers brought six hundred bananas to Beleghata this March for the second edition of Food For All, handing them out to residents in need of a quick, nutritious boost.

The drive keeps its approach simple by design: identify the need, show up with the essentials, and distribute them without ceremony. This edition kept that promise going.

header: Activity Hour - Fun Activities Workshop at Sunday School
short_summary: This joyful Sunday school session was packed with fun, laughter, and creative exploration.
long_writeup: This joyful Sunday school session was packed with fun, laughter, and creative exploration. Children participated in storytelling, group games, art-and-craft activities, and music-based learning, all designed to foster imagination, teamwork, and emotional expression. Volunteers created a safe and vibrant space where each child could engage freely and meaningfully. These playful yet thoughtful interactions encouraged bonding, built confidence, and reminded us of the importance of balancing learning with joy. The session not only brought smiles to young faces but also laid the groundwork for deeper social and emotional development.

header: Little Learners - Workshop at Sunday School
short_summary: Sunday School workshop with interactive sessions focused on learning, values, and fun activities.
long_writeup:
Four AquaTerra volunteers spent a March session at Pather Sathi running Little Learners, mixing interactive activities with simple lessons on values for thirty-five children.

The workshop kept things light and playful, but the underlying goal was steady: build habits of curiosity and kindness that the children could carry beyond the session itself.

header: Code and Connect - Computer Workshop at Sunday School
short_summary: In this edition of our computer workshop, Sunday school students were given guided exposure to essential digital tools and basic computer literacy.
long_writeup: In this edition of our computer workshop, Sunday school students were given guided exposure to essential digital tools and basic computer literacy. Volunteers helped the children navigate simple tasks like typing, using educational games, and understanding computer parts. For many, it was a first step toward bridging the digital divide. The workshop aimed to make technology less intimidating and more accessible, equipping young minds with foundational skills that could support their academic and personal growth. The joy and curiosity in the room reflected the power of early access to digital education.

header: Durga Puja Programme at Sunday School
short_summary: The Durga Puja Programme at Sunday School was a vibrant celebration of tradition, devotion, and togetherness.
long_writeup:
This October, five AquaTerra volunteers joined hands with Pather Sathi to close out weeks of Durga Puja preparations with one big celebration. Forty children took the stage to sing, perform, and share the art they had made in earlier sessions, turning the classroom into a festive hall for the afternoon.

There was pride in the air as kids who had spent weeks painting thalis and rehearsing songs finally got to show their families and friends what they had built. Volunteers stepped back and let the children lead, offering only quiet encouragement from the sidelines.

It was less a workshop and more a homecoming, a reminder of why the earlier weeks of effort mattered in the first place.

short_summary: Once Upon workshop captured hearts with every story told.
long_writeup:
Four AquaTerra volunteers brought stories to life at Lamp Open Shelter this September, gathering 25 children for an afternoon of Once Upon. What began as a simple read-aloud quickly turned into something more, with kids jumping in to guess endings, act out characters, and add their own twists to the tale.

Storytelling has a way of pulling even the shyest child forward, and this session was no exception. By the end, the room was full of raised hands and eager voices wanting to tell their own stories.

It was a quiet but meaningful reminder that sometimes the simplest tools, a story and a circle of listeners, leave the deepest impression.

short_summary: Sparked creativity and expression in our recent workshop.
long_writeup:
At Pather Sathi this August, three AquaTerra volunteers set up Art Alley, an afternoon where 45 children got their hands on paint, paper, and colour with no rules attached. The room quickly filled with chatter as kids compared their work and asked volunteers for tips on shading and mixing shades.

For many of the children, art class is a rare chance to make something just for the joy of it, and that showed in how reluctant they were to stop when time ran out. Volunteers moved table to table, offering encouragement rather than correction.

By the close of the session, the walls were lined with drawings each child was proud to call their own.

short_summary: Art workshop at Pather Sathi designed to spark creativity and engage children in hands-on learning
long_writeup:
This May, four AquaTerra volunteers ran Doodle and Draw at Pather Sathi, guiding 30 children through simple drawing exercises meant to build both confidence and creativity. Pencils and crayons were passed around as kids sketched everything from animals to their own imagined worlds.

The session leaned into play rather than instruction, letting children doodle freely while volunteers offered gentle nudges and praise. It was as much about self-expression as it was about technique.

By the end of the afternoon, every child had a page to take home, and a little more confidence in their own hand.

short_summary: Day 2 of food distribution drive offering meals to the needy with continued volunteer support.
long_writeup:
Four AquaTerra volunteers returned to the streets of Kolkata this April for the second day of the Food For All distribution drive, carrying 80 packed meals to hand out. The rhythm from Day 1 carried over, walking familiar routes and stopping wherever there was a need.

Each packet came with a brief exchange, a nod, a smile, sometimes just a moment of eye contact before moving on. It is in these small interactions that the drive finds its real purpose, beyond simply handing over food.

By the time the packets ran out, the volunteers had covered good ground and, more importantly, made sure no one nearby went without a meal that day.

short_summary: Introduced children to basic financial concepts through engaging activities and examples.
long_writeup:
One AquaTerra volunteer led Budget Basics at Pather Sathi this March, walking 25 children through the everyday idea of saving, spending, and planning ahead. Using relatable examples like pocket money and shopping lists, the session turned an often-dry topic into something the kids could actually picture themselves doing.

Questions came quickly once the ice broke, with children eager to share how they already handle small amounts of money at home. That curiosity made the workshop feel less like a lesson and more like a conversation.

It was a small session with a lasting goal: giving children tools they can carry well beyond the classroom.

short_summary: In collaboration with Sujata Child NGO, this Durga Puja workshop brought festive spirit and cultural connection to life for the children.
long_writeup:
This October, four AquaTerra volunteers partnered with Sujata Child NGO for a Durga Puja workshop that mixed mythology, art, and conversation. Thirty children heard the stories behind the festival before picking up crayons to draw idols and decorate their own thalis.

The real heart of the session came in the discussions that followed, where volunteers and children talked about courage and compassion, the values the festival is meant to celebrate. It gave the day a depth beyond just craft-making.

By the time the workshop wrapped, the room was full of finished artwork and a shared sense of what the festival stands for.

header: Skill Space - Workshop at Sunday School
short_summary: Sunday School workshop with activities blending fun, values, and interactive learning for kids.
long_writeup:
Four AquaTerra volunteers ran Skill Space at Pather Sathi's Sunday School this November, mixing games and group activities to hold the attention of 35 children for the whole session. The format kept shifting, from quick icebreakers to quieter group tasks, so no one had time to lose interest.

Volunteers wove in small lessons about teamwork and listening between the fun, letting the values sink in through play rather than lecture. Kids responded well to the mix, staying engaged right up to the closing activity.

It was a Sunday well spent, equal parts laughter and learning.

short_summary: South City International School students rock Morpheus Day 1 with Roots tees!
long_writeup:
Five AquaTerra volunteers kicked off Morpheus at South City International School this July, greeting a turnout of 300 students on the very first day. The Roots tees became an instant marker of the event, spotted across the courtyard as students settled in.

With numbers like that, the day had an energy of its own, volunteers moving between groups, answering questions, and keeping the momentum going. It set a strong tone for whatever the rest of Morpheus had in store.

Day 1 closed with the sense that this was only the beginning of something bigger on campus.

short_summary: The Waste Management Workshop aimed to instill eco-conscious habits among young participants through interactive games, demonstrations, and storytelling.
long_writeup:
Five AquaTerra volunteers brought Waste Wise to Ashok Hall School this August, using games and storytelling to walk 50 children through the basics of waste segregation and sustainable habits. Simple ideas like cloth bags and composting kitchen scraps were framed as everyday actions any child could try at home.

The demonstrations were the highlight, with kids sorting mock waste into the right bins and comparing notes on what surprised them most. It turned an abstract environmental issue into something tangible and personal.

Children left the session with more than facts, they left with a sense that their own choices genuinely matter.

short_summary: Interactive workshop to build children's speaking skills through games
long_writeup:
This April, four AquaTerra volunteers ran Speak Smart at Disha Foundation, using games and roleplay to help 35 children get more comfortable speaking in front of others. For many kids, just standing up to say a few sentences was the biggest hurdle of the day.

Volunteers kept the pressure low, framing every attempt as a win rather than a performance to get right. That approach coaxed even the quietest children into taking a turn by the end.

It was a small session with an outsized impact, giving children a bit more confidence in their own voice.

short_summary: Creative origami workshop where participants folded paper into art, learning focus and patience.
long_writeup:
Three AquaTerra volunteers led Fold and Fun at South Calcutta Inner Wheel School this December, guiding 40 children through paper folds that turned into cranes, boats, and boxes. What started as fumbled creases soon became careful, focused folding as kids got the hang of it.

Origami has a quiet way of teaching patience, and that showed as the room settled into concentrated silence between bursts of excitement over finished shapes. Volunteers moved around helping with trickier folds.

By the end, desks were covered in paper creations, each one a small proof of what a little patience can produce.

header: Ctrl+Create - Computer Workshop at Sunday School
short_summary: During this Sunday school workshop, children were introduced to foundational computer skills in an interactive and friendly environment.
long_writeup:
This July, three AquaTerra volunteers ran Ctrl+Create at Pather Sathi's Sunday School, introducing 30 children to a computer for many of them for the very first time. Volunteers walked the group through the basics, holding a mouse, finding icons, opening a simple program, one small step at a time.

What stood out was how quickly hesitation turned into curiosity. Children who started out unsure which button to click were soon asking to try things on their own, eager to see what else the screen could do.

It was a reminder that digital literacy starts small, and that the right first session can open a door that stays open.

short_summary: Distributed 20 liters of Rooh Afza sharbat to offer refreshment and relief from the heat.
long_writeup:
Four AquaTerra volunteers set up along Sarat Bose Road this March for the twenty-first round of Sharbat Seva, pouring out 20 litres of Rooh Afza to anyone passing through in the heat. Rickshaw pullers, shopkeepers, and pedestrians alike stopped for a cool glass and a brief moment of relief.

The drive has become something of a routine now, but each round still carries the same simple purpose, offering a small comfort to people working through the day's heat.

By the time the last glass was poured, the volunteers had covered a good stretch of the road and a lot of grateful smiles.
label_2: Glasses ready to quench their thirst

header: Tails and Treats - Feeding Stray Dogs 24.0
short_summary: Dog drive provided food, care, and comfort to furry friends in need.
long_writeup:
Eight AquaTerra volunteers turned out for the twenty-fourth Tails and Treats drive in Hazra this December, making sure 45 stray dogs got a proper meal and a bit of attention. With that many hands, the group could cover more ground, tracking down dogs tucked away in quieter corners of the neighbourhood.

Beyond the food, there was a lot of gentle petting and a few new friendships formed between volunteers and the neighbourhood's regulars. The dogs seemed to recognise the routine as much as the volunteers did.

It was a cold-weather reminder that care for strays doesn't take a break just because the season changes.

header: Colours Of Durga - Durga Puja Workshop at Sunday School 3.0
short_summary: The final session of the Durga Puja Workshop series was a vibrant celebration of culture, learning, and creativity.
long_writeup:
Two AquaTerra volunteers closed out the Durga Puja Workshop series at Pather Sathi this September with Colours of Durga, the third and final session. Twenty-five children took part in diya painting and thali decoration while volunteers retold the legends behind the festival.

With music playing and colours everywhere, the session had a celebratory feel that matched the occasion it was building toward. Children who had joined earlier sessions carried a familiarity into this one, making the closing feel earned rather than rushed.

It wrapped up the series on a high note, leaving the children with both finished crafts and a stronger sense of the culture behind them.

header: Merry Miracles Drive of Santa Mask Making Competition at Sunday School Day 3
short_summary: Day 3 of Merry Miracles: Kids crafted Santa masks, blending creativity with festive excitement.
long_writeup:
Four AquaTerra volunteers kept the Merry Miracles drive going into its third day at Pather Sathi this December, this time with a Santa mask making competition for 35 children. Scissors, glue, and cotton wool turned plain paper plates into a room full of grinning Santas.

The competitive spirit added an extra layer of fun, with kids proudly comparing their masks and volunteers handing out encouragement all around. Christmas excitement was clearly in the air.

It was a festive, hands-on afternoon that kept the Merry Miracles momentum building toward the days ahead.

short_summary: The fifth edition of Pather Sathi Sundarbans marked another impactful step towards deepening our connection with the Sundarbans and its resilient communities.
long_writeup:
The fifth edition of Pather Sathi Sundarbans, organized in collaboration with AquaTerra, marked yet another meaningful step in supporting one of India's most vulnerable and resilient regions. This initiative combined immediate relief efforts with long-term awareness.
Over the course of the program, 250+ medical checkups were conducted for residents across remote villages. Beyond healthcare, the initiative placed strong emphasis on awareness and education. Volunteers engaged communities in interactive sessions on climate resilience, waste management, and biodiversity conservation.
In partnership with local stakeholders, sustainable practices were promoted, including the use of cloth bags and safe drinking water through filtration methods. It was a steady, well-supported stop that kept building on the campaign's growing momentum across the city.

header: Wear & Write - Clothes & Notebooks Collection Campaign 11.0
short_summary: Segregation ensured clothes and notebooks reached those who needed them most.
long_writeup:
Five AquaTerra volunteers returned to Clubtown Greens this May for the eleventh edition of Wear & Write, collecting two kilograms of clothes and notebooks and carefully sorting them for distribution. The segregation step made sure donations would reach the right hands efficiently.

Volunteers worked through the collected items methodically, separating clothes by size and notebooks by condition to streamline what came next.

It was a quieter, more meticulous stop, but no less important for making sure every donation counted where it landed.

header: Wear & Write - Clothes & Notebooks Collection Campaign 10.0
short_summary: Joint drive for clothes and notebooks supported learning and living.
long_writeup:
In mid-May, four AquaTerra volunteers set up a collection point at Rajasthali, Park Circus, gathering clothes and notebooks from generous neighbours. It was a small, quick effort, but every bundle handed in meant one less child going without warm clothes or a fresh page to write on.

The team sorted donations on the spot, keeping the process simple for residents who dropped by between errands. What came together was 3 kgs of essentials, now on their way to families who needed exactly that.

header: Wear & Write - Clothes & Notebooks Collection Campaign 7.0
short_summary: Donated clothes and notebooks brought smiles to young learners.
long_writeup:
Seven volunteers turned out at Salarpuria Pearl, Gopalpur, this May for the seventh edition of Wear & Write, going door to door to collect clothes and notebooks for children who could use both. The response was steady, and by the end of the drive the team had gathered 3 kgs worth of donations.

What stood out wasn't the size of the haul but the consistency of neighbours showing up edition after edition. Sorted and packed, the donations were set to move straight to families in need, closing another small but meaningful loop.

header: Wear & Write - Clothes & Notebooks Collection Campaign 9.0
short_summary: Organised sorting of clothes and notebooks made donations more impactful.
long_writeup:
This May, three AquaTerra volunteers ran the ninth Wear & Write drive at Active Acres, collecting clothes and notebooks door to door. Careful sorting on-site meant nothing usable went to waste, and the effort added up to 5.5 kgs of donations by the end of the day.

Residents pitched in readily, and the team kept things organised so every item could reach a child who needed it. It's a rhythm the group has built drive after drive, one apartment complex at a time.

header: Wear & Write - Clothes & Notebooks Collection Campaign 14.0
short_summary: Volunteers sorted clothes and notebooks for smooth, fair distribution.
long_writeup:
The fourteenth Wear & Write drive brought four volunteers out across Kolkata in late May, collecting clothes and notebooks from households willing to share a little extra. By the time collection wrapped, the team had 6 kgs of donations ready to sort and send onward.

Each edition of this campaign has leaned on the same quiet consistency: knock, collect, sort, repeat. That steady approach is what let this round come together smoothly, with donations set to reach children who could use both a change of clothes and something to write in.

short_summary: Cold sharbat with a twist of lemon refreshed and delighted participants.
long_writeup:
Late May in Bagmari Market meant one thing for four AquaTerra volunteers: setting up jugs of chilled Rooh Afza sharbat for passersby caught in the heat. The fifteenth edition of Sharbat Seva kept the formula simple, cold drinks, a bit of lemon, and a lot of grateful smiles.

Over the course of the drive, the team poured out 20 litres of sharbat to market-goers and vendors alike. It's a small gesture, but on a scorching day in a busy market, a free cold drink goes a long way toward making someone's afternoon a little easier.

header: Wear & Write - Clothes & Notebooks Collection Campaign 4.0
short_summary: Drive gathered clothes and notebooks to help underprivileged children.
long_writeup:
Six volunteers spent early May going door to door at Anandam Apartment, Bangur, collecting clothes and notebooks for the fourth round of Wear & Write. Residents responded warmly, contributing what they could to support children who needed both.

By the end of the drive, the team had gathered 3.5 kgs of donations, sorted and ready to be passed along. It's the kind of quiet, repeatable effort that adds up over time, one apartment block and one contribution at a time.

short_summary: Cold, spiced sharbat was the highlight of the drive.
long_writeup:
At Bangur Shani-Kali Mandir this May, six AquaTerra volunteers set up for the eighth Sharbat Seva drive, ladling out cold Rooh Afza to everyone passing through. The temple crowd made for a steady stream of thirsty visitors glad for the break.

By the time the jugs ran dry, the team had served 20 litres of sharbat. Nothing fancy, just cold drinks handed out with a smile, but on a hot day near a busy temple, it made a real difference to those who stopped by.

header: Wear & Write - Clothes & Notebooks Collection Campaign 13.0
short_summary: Clothes and notebooks drive empowered young minds and warmed many hearts.
long_writeup:
The thirteenth Wear & Write drive saw three volunteers canvassing Kolkata in late May, collecting clothes and notebooks from willing households. As with earlier editions, the approach was simple: ask, collect, sort, and pass along.

The day's effort brought in 5 kgs of donations, another steady contribution toward the campaign's ongoing goal of pairing warm clothing with the tools children need for school. Small drives like this one keep building toward a larger, cumulative impact.

short_summary: Multi-flavour sharbat served cold, adding flavour to the day.
long_writeup:
Six volunteers took the eleventh Sharbat Seva drive to Manicktolla and Kankurgachi in late May, serving up chilled Rooh Afza in a few different flavours to keep things interesting for the crowd. It was another hot day, and the response from locals made that clear.

By the end of the shift, the team had handed out 20 litres of sharbat to residents grateful for a cold drink. Simple as it is, the drive has become a reliable bit of relief during Kolkata's harshest summer stretches.

short_summary: Volunteers delighted crowds with icy red & green sharbat at the drive.
long_writeup:
Outside Trisha Impressions in Kankurgachi, six AquaTerra volunteers ran the third Sharbat Seva drive, pouring out glasses of icy red and green Rooh Afza for anyone walking by. The colours drew attention, but it was the cold relief that kept people coming back for seconds.

Over the course of the drive, the team distributed 20 litres of sharbat, turning a routine market stretch into a small pocket of relief from the heat.

short_summary: Icy floral sharbat revived spirits and beat the heat.
long_writeup:
Five volunteers set up near Bhagya Lakshmi in late May for the ninth Sharbat Seva drive, serving cold, floral-scented Rooh Afza to a steady stream of visitors. The heat made the offer an easy sell, and the queue rarely thinned out.

By the time the drive wrapped, the team had poured 20 litres of sharbat for the neighbourhood. It's a small ritual by now, one that locals seem to look forward to each time the volunteers show up.

short_summary: Cold rose and mint sharbat quenched thirst and spread smiles all around.
long_writeup:
Seven volunteers, the largest team of the campaign so far, lined up along Sarat Bose Road near Hazra for the fourth Sharbat Seva drive, serving rose and mint Rooh Afza to passersby. With more hands on deck, the line moved quickly and few people left without a glass.

The drive closed out with 20 litres distributed, another hot afternoon made a little more bearable for commuters and shoppers passing through one of the city's busier stretches.

header: Wear and Share - Clothes Collection Drive 8.0
short_summary: Shared warmth through donated clothes at the collection drive.
long_writeup:
In mid-July, five volunteers ran the eighth Wear and Share drive at Raghav Residency, going door to door for clothing donations. Residents responded generously despite the season, and the team kept the collection process quick and organised.

By the end of the day, 4 kgs of clothes had been gathered, ready to be sorted and passed on to families who could use them. It's a modest number, but for the people on the receiving end, it's a real difference.

short_summary: Colourful layered sharbat served cold to brighten everyone's day.
long_writeup:
Five volunteers took the sixth Sharbat Seva drive to Ballygunge Circular Road, pouring layered, colourful glasses of chilled Rooh Afza for anyone who stopped by. The visual appeal drew a few curious onlookers, but the real draw was relief from the heat.

The team ended the drive having served 20 litres of sharbat, another dose of cold comfort delivered to a busy Kolkata street on a warm May day.

header: Wear and Share - Clothes Collection Drive 7.0
short_summary: Clothes and notebooks collected to make education more accessible.
long_writeup:
Back at Rajasthali, Park Circus, six volunteers ran the seventh Wear and Share drive in late May, collecting both clothes and notebooks from residents who'd supported earlier rounds too. Familiar faces made the process quicker, with donations coming in steadily through the day.

By the close of the drive, the team had gathered 3 kgs of items, sorted and set to reach children who need both warm clothing and school supplies. Repeat visits like this one show how a neighbourhood can build a habit of giving.

header: Wear and Share - Clothes Collection Drive 3.0
short_summary: Clothing drive united hearts to help families in need.
long_writeup:
Four volunteers spent a day in mid-May at Urbana, Madurdaha, running the third Wear and Share drive and collecting clothes from residents floor by floor. Turnout was strong, and the team kept pace sorting items as they came in.

The drive closed with 6 kgs of clothing collected, all headed toward families who could use an extra layer or a fresh outfit. It's the kind of effort that relies entirely on neighbours choosing to share a little more than they need.

header: Wear and Share - Clothes Collection Drive 2.0
short_summary: Donated clothes spread comfort and kindness across the community.
long_writeup:
Early May brought three volunteers to Ganges Garden Phase 1 for the second Wear and Share drive, collecting clothes from residents willing to clear out their closets for a good cause. The pace was steady through the morning, with donations trickling in from block after block.

By the end of the drive, 3 kgs of clothing had been gathered and sorted for onward distribution. Small as the haul was, it added another layer of support for families who needed it.

header: Wear and Share - Clothes Collection Drive 1.0
short_summary: Clothes collection drive brought warmth and hope to those in need.
long_writeup:
The very first Wear and Share drive kicked off at Ganges Garden Phase 1 in early May, with five volunteers going block to block asking residents to donate clothes they no longer needed. As the opening edition of the campaign, it set the tone for what would become a recurring effort.

The team collected 4 kgs of clothing by day's end, a modest start that would go on to be repeated across the city in the weeks that followed.

short_summary: Summer smiles with frosty fruit-infused sharbat for everyone.
long_writeup:
Five volunteers set up near the swimming pool in Salt Lake for the twelfth Sharbat Seva drive, handing out fruit-infused, chilled Rooh Afza to swimmers and passersby cooling off from the May heat. The poolside crowd made for an easy, appreciative audience.

By the end of the session, the team had distributed 20 litres of sharbat, one more stop in a campaign that's found its rhythm serving cold relief wherever Kolkata's heat bites hardest.

header: Wear & Write - Clothes & Notebooks Collection Campaign 15.0
short_summary: Clothes and notebooks drive spread warmth and knowledge alike.
long_writeup:
A year on from earlier editions, seven volunteers returned to Salarpuria Pearl, Gopalpur, in May 2025 for the fifteenth Wear & Write drive, collecting clothes and notebooks once again from a community that's clearly gotten used to the ask. The response showed it, with donations arriving steadily through the day.

The team wrapped up with 6 kgs collected, sorted and ready to move on to children who'll make good use of both the clothing and the notebooks. Fifteen editions in, the campaign keeps finding new households ready to give.

header: Wear and Share - Clothes Collection Drive 5.0
short_summary: Volunteers sorted donated clothes with care for efficient distribution.
long_writeup:
In mid-May, five volunteers worked the Govinda Mahal Flat Owners Association for the fifth Wear and Share drive, collecting clothing donations from residents across the building. The team sorted items carefully as they came in, keeping the process organised for quick redistribution.

The day ended with 3.5 kgs of clothes collected, another small but steady contribution toward the campaign's larger goal of getting warm clothing to families who need it most.

header: Wear & Write - Clothes & Notebooks Collection Campaign 5.0
short_summary: Clothes and notebooks drive spread warmth and knowledge alike.
long_writeup:
Six volunteers spent early May at Sweta Apartment, Bangur, running the fifth Wear & Write drive and collecting both clothes and notebooks from residents there. It was a quieter round in terms of volume, but every contribution counted toward the cause.

The team gathered 2.5 kgs of donations by the end of the day, sorted and set aside for children who could use a bit of both warmth and school supplies. Even smaller drives like this one add up across a campaign built on repetition.

short_summary: Joy, laughter, and twinkling lights made Christmas celebrations truly magical.
long_writeup:
Just before Christmas 2022, four AquaTerra volunteers headed to Disha Foundation to run Merry Moments, a festive workshop full of songs, games, and a bit of holiday sparkle. Forty children joined in, and it didn't take long for the room to fill with laughter.

Between the decorations and the activities, the afternoon turned into exactly the kind of joyful break the season calls for. For the volunteers, it was a reminder that sometimes the simplest gestures, a song, a game, a shared laugh, carry the most warmth.

short_summary: Students learned basic first aid to handle urgent situations.
long_writeup:
In August 2022, three AquaTerra volunteers ran Safety First at Shanti Rani Primary School, walking forty children through the basics of first aid, from treating small cuts to knowing when to call for help. The lessons were kept simple and hands-on, suited to the age group in the room.

What the volunteers hoped to leave behind wasn't just information but a bit of confidence: that these kids now know a few things to do in a moment that matters. Practical skills like these tend to stick, long after the workshop itself is over.

short_summary: Creativity bloomed as children painted, crafted, and played at the art workshop.
long_writeup:
Three volunteers brought Free Flow, an open-ended art workshop, to Pather Sathi in March 2023, letting thirty children loose with paint, paper, and whatever else sparked their imagination. There was no single project to finish, just space to create.

The result was a room full of colour and concentration, kids trying things out without worrying about getting it right. For an afternoon, that kind of unstructured creativity was the whole point, and it showed in how reluctant everyone was to clean up.

short_summary: Students explored acting, voice, and movement in an engaging, creativity-packed drama workshop.
long_writeup:
Seven volunteers, the biggest team so far, launched the Drama Workshop series at Disha Foundation in July 2022, introducing thirty students to the basics of acting, voice projection, and stage movement. It was a first attempt at something new, and the energy in the room reflected that.

Students who'd never performed before found themselves improvising scenes and finding their voice, literally, by the end of the session. It set the tone for the editions that would follow, proving there was real appetite for this kind of creative outlet.

short_summary: Maths tables workshop made learning multiplication easy and fun.
long_writeup:
Three volunteers ran Table Time at School on Wheels - HUHT in May 2023, turning multiplication tables into something closer to a game than a chore for thirty children. Chants, quick drills, and a bit of friendly competition kept the energy up.

Maths can be a tough sell for a classroom of restless kids, but breaking it into a fun, repeatable rhythm made the numbers stick a little easier. By the end, most of the room was reciting tables they'd been struggling with just an hour before.

header: Respect and Reach - Old Age Home drive 3.0
short_summary: Students brought joy, gifts, and warmth to residents during the Old Age Home drive.
long_writeup:
For the third Respect and Reach visit, five volunteers spent time at Urban Shelter For Homeless in May 2023, sitting with thirty elderly residents, sharing conversation, and handing out small gifts. It wasn't a grand gesture, just company and attention for people who don't always get enough of either.

The visit leaned on something simple: showing up, listening, and making people feel seen. For residents who spend most days without visitors, an afternoon like this can mean more than the gifts themselves.

short_summary: Cricket workshop honed batting, bowling, and fielding skills for young players.
long_writeup:
Seven volunteers took Bat and Ball to Pather Sathi in May 2023, running thirty-five children through the fundamentals of cricket: proper batting stance, bowling technique, and sharper fielding. The session had the feel of a proper practice, drills and all.

For a sport this popular in Kolkata, the workshop was less about teaching something unfamiliar and more about sharpening what these kids already loved. By the end, there were plenty of proud demonstrations of a cleaner cover drive or a tighter yorker.

short_summary: Workshop built curiosity and strengthened students' basic science knowledge.
long_writeup:
Three volunteers ran Science Time at School on Wheels - HUHT in May 2023, walking twenty-five children through foundational science concepts using simple explanations and a few hands-on demonstrations. Questions came quickly once the ideas started clicking.

The goal wasn't to cover everything, just to build curiosity and give students a stronger footing in ideas they'd meet again in the classroom. Judging by how many hands stayed up through the session, that curiosity was well and truly sparked.

short_summary: Little artists splashed colors and creativity at the fun-filled children's art workshop.
long_writeup:
Three volunteers ran Colour Play at Pather Sathi in January 2023, giving thirty-five children free rein with paints and brushes for an afternoon of pure creative mess. There was no right answer here, just colour, paper, and imagination.

What started as a simple painting session turned into a room full of proud young artists holding up their work. Moments like these are a reminder that creative play doesn't need much structure to leave a real impression.

short_summary: Students honed acting skills and unleashed creativity at the vibrant school drama workshop.
long_writeup:
By the fourth edition of the Drama Workshop series in August 2022, six volunteers had a rhythm down, guiding thirty children at Disha Foundation through scene work, improvisation, and stage confidence. Familiar faces from earlier sessions came back sharper and bolder.

The progression across editions was clear: kids who'd been shy in the first workshop were now volunteering to go first. That kind of visible growth is what kept the series going strong through the year.

short_summary: Students explored painting, sketching, and design at the art workshop.
long_writeup:
Two volunteers ran Art Adventure at Pather Sathi in May 2023, guiding forty children through painting, sketching, and simple design exercises. With just two volunteers managing a big group, the session leaned on keeping activities simple and easy to follow.

Even with the smaller team, the turnout made for a lively, crowded room of kids eager to try each new exercise. It was proof that enthusiasm on both sides can make up for a smaller volunteer count.

short_summary: ICCV Science Exhibition inspired curiosity and scientific learning for all.
long_writeup:
Four volunteers set up the ICCV science exhibition at Pather Sathi in April 2023, bringing hands-on exhibits and demonstrations to forty-five curious children. The format gave kids room to explore at their own pace, moving between stations and asking questions as they went.

Rather than a straight lecture, the exhibition let science speak for itself through experiments kids could see and touch. That approach paid off in a room buzzing with questions long after the formal explanations had ended.

short_summary: Kids explored shapes, colors, and imagination in the lively art workshop.
long_writeup:
Two volunteers ran Pastel Play at Pather Sathi in January 2023, introducing forty-five children to shapes, colour blending, and open-ended drawing with pastels. It was a big group for a small team, but the structure of the activity kept things manageable.

Kids leaned into the freedom the medium offered, mixing colours and inventing shapes without much guidance needed. The session wrapped with a wall of pastel drawings, each one a little different from the last.

short_summary: Christmas cheer filled the air with carols, lights, and joyful celebrations for all.
long_writeup:
Four volunteers brought Season's Magic to Pather Sathi in December 2022, filling the space with carols, festive decorations, and games for forty-five children ahead of the holidays. The mood was pure celebration from start to finish.

For many of the kids, it was a rare chance to mark the season with the kind of festivity they don't always get to experience. Between the singing and the games, the workshop turned into one of the year's most cheerful outings for the volunteers as well.

short_summary: Food that fills stomachs, love that touches hearts.
long_writeup:
A single AquaTerra volunteer took on the Food Distribution Drive at Lighthouse for the Blind in November 2022, personally handing out thirty food packets to residents there. It was a smaller-scale effort, but no less meaningful for it.

Sometimes impact doesn't need a crowd, just someone willing to show up with something useful in hand. For the residents who received a warm meal that day, the size of the team mattered far less than the fact that someone came at all.

short_summary: A season of love, giving, and warmth—Christmas united hearts in festive spirit.
long_writeup:
Three volunteers ran Jolly Vibes at Ektara in December 2022, gathering thirty children for an afternoon of Christmas songs, games, and festive spirit. The small team kept things intimate, with plenty of one-on-one moments between volunteers and kids.

It's easy for a holiday workshop to feel like just another event, but the warmth in the room that day made it clear this one landed differently. Children left with the kind of festive glow that's hard to manufacture and easy to remember.

short_summary: Drama workshop brought stories to life, boosting confidence, teamwork, and stage presence.
long_writeup:
Seven volunteers returned to Disha Foundation in August 2022 for the second Drama Workshop, working with thirty-five children on storytelling, teamwork, and stage presence. Building on the first session, the group tackled slightly more ambitious scenes.

What came through most was the shift in confidence: kids who'd hesitated to speak up in the opening workshop were now stepping into character without much prompting. That kind of quick growth is exactly what kept the series worth running.

short_summary: Laughter, learning, and improvisation made the drama workshop a hit among budding performers.
long_writeup:
Seven volunteers ran the third Drama Workshop at Disha Foundation in August 2022, leading thirty-five children through improvisation games and short scenes. By this point in the series, the kids knew the drill and dove in with noticeably less hesitation.

Improvisation games drew the biggest laughs, turning what could have been a straightforward lesson into an afternoon of genuine fun. Three editions in, it was clear the format had found its footing with this group.

short_summary: Rising temperatures and melting ice show the harsh impact of global warming. Teaching children how to take preventative action.
long_writeup:
Climate change can feel like a huge, distant idea, so this April four AquaTerra volunteers brought it down to earth for the kids at Pather Sathi. Through simple explanations of melting ice and rising temperatures, the workshop helped children connect everyday choices to the bigger picture.

Rather than just listing facts, the session focused on prevention, giving 40 children practical habits they could actually carry home. It was a small step, but one aimed at raising a generation that thinks a little harder about the planet.

short_summary: Waste to Wealth workshop turned scrap into creative, useful products.
long_writeup:
Old boxes, bottle caps, and scraps of fabric got a second life at Loretto Rainbow Home this August, as six AquaTerra volunteers ran the Waste to Wealth workshop. The idea was simple: show children that things we usually throw away can become something useful and even beautiful.

25 kids spent the session turning trash into craft, picking up both an environmental lesson and a bit of hands-on creativity along the way. It was messy, playful, and exactly the kind of learning that sticks.

short_summary: Dreamcatcher making sparked imagination and artistic expression.
long_writeup:
There's something quietly special about watching kids thread string and beads into their own dreamcatcher. That was the scene at Pather Sathi this March, where three AquaTerra volunteers guided 40 children through the craft, step by careful step.

Beyond the finished pieces, the workshop gave the children room to express themselves and take pride in something made entirely by their own hands. It was a small, colorful afternoon of imagination doing exactly what it does best.

location: Loreto Day School Elliot road (collab w/ WoC)
short_summary: Participants learned coping skills and mindfulness at the mental health workshop.
long_writeup:
Mental health conversations don't come naturally to most classrooms, which is exactly why this workshop mattered. In collaboration with WoC, four AquaTerra volunteers spent the day at Loreto Day School, Elliot Road this August, walking 40 children through simple coping strategies and mindfulness exercises.

The goal wasn't to solve everything in one session, but to plant the idea that it's okay to talk about feelings and that there are tools to manage them. Judging by how engaged the kids stayed, that seed found good ground.

short_summary: Life in a Bottle workshop taught creating self-sustaining terrariums with care.
long_writeup:
Building a tiny self-sustaining world inside a bottle sounds like magic to a child, and that's more or less what happened at Pather Sathi this August. Three AquaTerra volunteers guided 40 children through layering soil, stones, and small plants into their own terrariums.

Beyond the fun of getting hands dirty, the session quietly introduced ideas about ecosystems and responsibility, since each child now had a little living thing to look after. Simple materials, but a lasting lesson in care.

short_summary: From script to stage, the drama workshop nurtured talent and passion for theatrical arts.
long_writeup:
Scripts, expressions, and a bit of stage fright turned into confidence over the course of Drama Workshop 5.0 at Disha Foundation this August. Five AquaTerra volunteers worked with 30 children, moving them from reading lines to actually performing them.

Across the fifth edition of this recurring workshop, the focus stayed on building comfort in front of an audience as much as on the craft itself. For many of the kids, it was likely their first taste of what it feels like to hold a room's attention, even if just for a scene.

short_summary: Students learned basic first aid to handle urgent situations.
long_writeup:
Knowing what to do in the first few minutes of an emergency can make all the difference, and that's the gap this workshop tried to close. Two AquaTerra volunteers spent the day at Pather Sathi this April walking 25 children through the basics of first aid.

From simple bandaging to knowing when to seek help, the session kept things practical and age-appropriate. It was a short workshop with a long-term aim: giving kids the confidence to act, not freeze, when it counts.

short_summary: Students learned grammar rules and usage in an engaging workshop.
long_writeup:
Grammar rarely gets kids excited, but that was the challenge two AquaTerra volunteers took on at Pather Sathi this April. Working with 35 children, they broke down grammar rules and usage into an engaging, less intimidating format.

The session aimed to strengthen a foundational skill that often gets overlooked in informal learning settings. Small group energy and patient explanations made the difference, turning a subject many dread into one the kids actually leaned into.

short_summary: Colourful sharbat drive quenched thirst and spread joy.
long_writeup:
Summer in Kolkata doesn't ask nicely, so on this April day four AquaTerra volunteers showed up at Balaji Apartment with something better than words of comfort: cold sharbat. This was the 30th edition of the ongoing Sharbat Seva drive, and by now the routine has become a small tradition.

20 litres of Rooh Afza went around to residents looking for a moment of relief from the heat. It's a simple gesture, but one repeated often enough that it's started to mean something more than just a drink.

header: Art Therapy - Creative Arts and Drawing Workshop
short_summary: Creativity bloomed as children painted, crafted, and played at the art workshop.
long_writeup:
Colours have a way of loosening things up, and that was clear at Hope Foundation this June, where four AquaTerra volunteers ran an art therapy session built around painting, craft, and play. 40 children took part, each finding their own way into the activities.

There was no single right answer expected from anyone, which is exactly what made the afternoon work. Sometimes the most therapeutic thing a child can do is simply make something with their hands and be told it's good.

header: Food For All - Food Distribution Drive 13.0
short_summary: Food drive brought nourishment and hope to many lives.
long_writeup:
The 13th round of Food For All brought five AquaTerra volunteers to Salt Lake this April, continuing a drive that's become one of the team's steadiest commitments. 600 bananas were handed out, a small but reliable source of nutrition for people who need it.

There's nothing flashy about a banana drive, and that's rather the point. It's consistency, not spectacle, that keeps a project like this meaningful edition after edition.

short_summary: Chilled sharbat served as a refreshing treat on a hot day.
long_writeup:
By the time Sharbat Seva reached its 28th edition, four AquaTerra volunteers had the routine down: show up at Pritam Apartment, pour generously, and let the heat do the rest of the convincing. This April run was no different, with 20 litres of Rooh Afza going around to grateful residents.

It's a quick visit each time, but the kind that leaves a cool aftertaste and a reminder that someone thought of the neighbourhood on a scorching day.

short_summary: Sharbat drive turned a hot day into a cool celebration.
long_writeup:
Three AquaTerra volunteers carried the Sharbat Seva drive into its 31st edition this April, this time setting up in Dakhinashwar. As always, the offering was simple: 20 litres of cold Rooh Afza for anyone looking to escape the heat for a minute.

What started as one drive has now become a running series, and each stop adds one more neighbourhood to the list of places that got a small, cool break in their day.

short_summary: Day 2 of Nature x English brought stories, leaves, poems & purpose—learning rooted in the outdoors!
long_writeup:
Leaves, poems, and a bit of open air made up the second day of Nature x English at Ek Tara this June, led by four AquaTerra volunteers. Rather than keeping the 35 children indoors with textbooks, the session took learning outside, letting nature itself become part of the lesson.

Stories were built around what the kids could touch and see, tying language skills to the world right in front of them. It made for a session that felt less like a lesson and more like an adventure with a purpose.

header: Food For All - Food Distribution Drive 14.0
short_summary: Sharing meals with love, the food drive touched countless hearts.
long_writeup:
At Northern Park, four AquaTerra volunteers carried out the fourteenth edition of the Food For All drive, handing out 600 bananas along with other food items to those who needed a meal that day. The line moved steadily as volunteers worked through the crowd.
Each handout was brief, but the volunteers made a point of greeting people by more than just a passing nod, keeping the exchange personal rather than transactional.
Drives like this one are part of a long-running effort by AquaTerra to make sure no one in the area goes without a meal on the days the team shows up.

short_summary: Plantation of 50+ saplings, nurtured nature's balance.
long_writeup:
In Gachtala, twelve AquaTerra volunteers came together for the sixteenth edition of the Grow Green plantation drive, putting in the work to plant around a hundred saplings across the area. It was one of the larger turnouts for the initiative.
Volunteers dug, planted, and watered in teams, moving steadily across the plot until every sapling was in the ground. The scale of the group made quick, coordinated work of what would otherwise have taken far longer.
Drives like this one are AquaTerra's quiet bet on the future, small trees today that the volunteers hope will grow into something the whole neighbourhood benefits from.

header: Tails and Treats - Feeding Stray Dogs 15.0
short_summary: Dog drives provided food, shelter, and care for strays in need.
long_writeup:
Across Kolkata, five AquaTerra volunteers carried out the fifteenth edition of the stray dog feeding drive, making sure about sixty dogs were fed and looked after for the day. The team moved through familiar routes, stopping wherever the strays gathered.
Some dogs recognized the volunteers on sight, while others kept a cautious distance until the food was set down. Patience mattered as much as the meals themselves.

Fifteen kids got through the lesson, leaving with a slightly firmer grip on how to string a sentence together.

short_summary: 25+ kids attended this workshop where the volunteers taught kids about digital safety
long_writeup:
AquaTerra volunteers ran a Digital Safety Workshop at Pather Saathi, walking a group of kids through the basics of staying safe online: what to share, what not to, and how to spot something that doesn't look right. The topic is less hands-on than a craft session, so the volunteers leaned on examples and questions to keep it engaging.

More than 25 kids attended, coming away with a clearer sense of how to handle themselves on the internet.

long_writeup:
Three AquaTerra volunteers ran Tails and Treats at Dobson Lane, walking the area with a stock of biscuits for the dogs and cows that call the street home. It's a short, simple kind of drive, more about showing up consistently than doing anything elaborate.

Over the hour, more than 10 dogs and cows were fed, a quiet, steady bit of care for the animals that share the neighborhood.
